result: The authors identify four adipocyte subpopulations in mPRAT through snRNA-seq, including a distinct Ucp1-&Cidea+ subpopulation (mPRAT-ad2) that is absent in iBAT. Trajectory analysis reveals a progressive brown-to-white transition during postnatal life, with decreasing proportions of mPRAT-ad1 and ad2 and increasing proportions of ad3 and ad4 from 1 to 6 months. Gene expression patterns along the pseudo-timeline show decreasing BA markers and increasing WA markers.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes 'there is overall a disconnection between single nucleus RNA-seq data and the lineage chasing data' and states 'No specific markers of this population have been validated by staining.' Reviewer 3 acknowledges the identification of the mPRAT-ad2 population but notes 'the limited sequencing depth of single nuclei somewhat lessens the impact of these findings.' The editor summarizes that evidence is 'convincing, although limited sequencing depth of single nuclei...somewhat lessens the impact.'

result: Using UCP1-lineage tracing (Ucp1CreERT2;Ai14 mice), the authors demonstrate that 61.8% of tdTomato+ cells in puPRAT lost UCP1 expression by 2 months, compared to only 7.5% in pvPRAT, indicating regional differences in brown-to-white conversion. Morphological analysis shows tdTomato+&UCP1- adipocytes display unilocular lipid droplets characteristic of white adipocytes. Immunostaining reveals that 34% and 23% of these whitened adipocytes express CYP2E1 and ALDH1A1, respectively, markers of mature white adipocyte subpopulations.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 requests validation of the lineage tracing system, stating 'The UCP1Cre-ERT2; Ai14 system should be validated by showing Tomato and UCP1 co-staining right after the Tamoxifen treatment.' This suggests concern about the specificity and efficiency of the lineage tracing approach. Reviewer 2 also notes the 'disconnection between single nucleus RNA-seq data and the lineage chasing data,' indicating that the integration of these two lines of evidence needs strengthening.

result: Cold exposure restores UCP1 expression and thermogenic phenotype in mPRAT, particularly in the mPRAT-ad2 subpopulation. The proportion of tdTomato+&UCP1- adipocytes decreased significantly after cold exposure in both puPRAT and pvPRAT. snRNA-seq analysis shows that mPRAT-ad2 cells completely disappeared after cold exposure while mPRAT-ad1 doubled, with no enhanced cell death observed. The authors conclude that new brown adipocytes induced by cold were mainly derived from UCP1- adipocytes rather than de novo ASPC differentiation in puPRAT.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'It would be nice to provide more evidence to support the conclusion shown in lines 243 to 245 "These results indicated that new BAs induced by cold exposure were mainly derived from UCP1- adipocytes rather than de novo ASPC differentiation in puPRAT". Pdgfra-negative progenitor cells may also contribute to these new beige adipocytes.' This indicates the reviewers find the evidence insufficient to exclude alternative explanations for the origin of cold-recruited brown adipocytes.

result: The mPRAT-ad2 subpopulation has a transcriptome distinct from subcutaneous beige adipocytes (iWAT BeAs). At room temperature, little overlap exists between mPRAT and iWAT adipocyte subpopulations. Upon cold exposure, while iWAT BeAs show correspondence with a fraction of mPRAT-ad1, most mPRAT-ad1 adipocytes that arise from mPRAT-ad2 have a distinct transcriptome from cold-induced BeAs in iWAT. Even after cold exposure, thermogenic brown adipocytes in mPRAT are more similar to iBAT than iWAT.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly acknowledges this finding, stating 'The combination of UCP1-lineage tracing with the single nuclei analysis allowed the authors to identify four populations of adipocytes with differing thermogenic potential, including an "whitened" adipocyte (mPRAT-ad2) that retains the capacity to rapidly revert to a brown phenotype upon cold exposure.' The editor notes the work 'presents a valuable finding on the process of brown-to-white adipogenic transdifferentiation.' No reviewer challenges the transcriptomic distinctiveness of mPRAT-ad2 from iWAT beige adipocytes.

result: The authors profiled 11,708 nuclei from mPRAT and 31,079 nuclei from iBAT across three time points (1, 2, and 6 months). Six cell type clusters were identified in mPRAT and similar cell types in iBAT. Four adipocyte subpopulations were identified in both depots. Module score analysis revealed that mPRAT-ad1 was similar to iBAT brown adipocyte subpopulations (iBAT-ad1, 2, 3), while mPRAT-ad3 and ad4 were similar to iBAT-ad4.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes 'the limited sequencing depth of single nuclei somewhat lessens the impact of these findings,' which directly questions the robustness of the snRNA-seq data. The editor echoes this concern, stating the evidence is 'convincing, although limited sequencing depth of single nuclei...somewhat lessens the impact.' This suggests the reviewers accept the general findings but have reservations about the depth of the sequencing data.

result: ASPC populations in mPRAT, iBAT, lPRAT, and iWAT were characterized and subclustered into distinct subpopulations (FAPs and preadipocytes at different differentiation stages). Co-clustering revealed high similarity between mPRAT and iBAT ASPCs, suggesting they may give rise to similar adipocyte types. The proportions of ASPC subpopulations remained relatively unchanged after cold exposure in all depots examined.
evaluation: No reviewer raises concerns about the ASPC characterization or the finding that ASPC proportions remain unchanged after cold exposure. These findings are presented as supporting data for the main conclusions about adipocyte transdifferentiation rather than de novo adipogenesis being the primary mechanism of cold-induced browning.

result: The authors characterized lateral PRAT (lPRAT), identifying four adipocyte subpopulations and three macrophage subpopulations. Comparison with epididymal WAT (eWAT) revealed only partial overlap in adipocyte and ASPC populations, and very different macrophage populations. The cellular composition of lPRAT showed aging signatures, with decreased adipocyte proportion and increased macrophage proportion from 2 to 6 months.
evaluation: No reviewer challenges the lPRAT characterization. This depot serves as a control showing that not all perirenal adipose tissue undergoes brown-to-white conversion, and the reviewers do not question these findings. The characterization is treated as supporting context for understanding the unique properties of mPRAT.

result: UCP1 immunostaining revealed uneven distribution of UCP1-expressing brown adipocytes in mPRAT, with more intense staining in the perivascular region (pvPRAT) compared to the periureter region (puPRAT) in both juvenile and adult mice. UCP1 staining decreased in adult compared to juvenile mPRAT and was absent from lPRAT.
evaluation: No reviewer questions these anatomical observations. The regional heterogeneity within mPRAT is accepted as context for understanding the differential extent of brown-to-white conversion in different regions of the depot.

result: Using PdgfraCreERT2;Ai14 mice, the authors quantified the contribution of ASPC-derived adipocytes to cold-recruited brown adipocytes. In puPRAT, ASPC-derived BAs increased 2.3-fold while total cold-recruited BAs increased 10-fold. In pvPRAT, the increases were 4.4-fold and 2.2-fold, respectively. All adipocytes in both regions were 100% tdTomato+, indicating complete derivation from Pdgfra-expressing cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 specifically questions this conclusion, stating 'It would be nice to provide more evidence to support the conclusion...Pdgfra-negative progenitor cells may also contribute to these new beige adipocytes.' This directly challenges the interpretation that the difference between ASPC-derived and total cold-recruited adipocytes can be attributed solely to conversion from UCP1- adipocytes, suggesting alternative progenitor sources were not adequately ruled out.

result: snRNA-seq analysis of mPRAT, iBAT, and iWAT after cold exposure revealed depot-specific responses. In mPRAT, cold exposure dramatically altered adipocyte composition with mPRAT-ad2 disappearing and mPRAT-ad1 doubling. In iBAT, all adipocyte subpopulations increased BA marker expression and showed conversions among Ucp1+ subpopulations. In iWAT, cold-specific subpopulations emerged including BeAs (iWAT-ad1) and a lipogenic subpopulation (iWAT-ad2). Cell-cell communication analysis showed different patterns across depots under both room temperature and cold exposure conditions.
evaluation: No reviewer challenges these comparative findings across depots. Reviewer 3 notes 'the combination of well-executed lineage tracing with comprehensive cross-depot single-nuclei presented in this manuscript could still serve as a useful reference for the field,' indicating acceptance of the cross-depot comparisons despite concerns about sequencing depth.
